atAGlance: Phở tái is beef phở with very thin rare beef slices that finish cooking in the hot broth. It is clean, aromatic, and more tender than the well-done beef version.
whatItIs: Phở tái is beef phở with thin rare beef slices added just before serving, so the hot broth finishes them in the bowl. It gives you tender beef without making the soup heavy.
howToEnjoy: Let the beef sit in the broth for a moment, then taste before adding chili or lime. Choose phở chín if you want fully cooked beef from the start.
howLocalsOrder: Phở tái is the order when you want rare beef, so say the full name instead of just phở. Add lime, herbs, and chili after tasting the beef broth; ask chín if you decide you want cooked meat instead.
worthKnowing: Tái means rare or lightly cooked. In a hot bowl of phở, the beef finishes cooking at the table, which is why locals order it confidently.
goodToKnow: If rare beef makes you nervous, order phở chín instead. The broth should still be hot enough to soften the beef at the table.

orderLine.vietnamese: Cho tôi một tô phở tái.
